samples.summary: Copy-service comment (and the active template-gallery TODO) still assert that `doc` images live at the bucket root; the new share-link upload makes workspace-scoped URLs an ordinary thing for doc content to hold
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/src/document/document-copy.service.ts:432` — "`doc` images are uploaded to the bucket root (`docsImageUploader` → `POST /images`), so there is normally nothing here to re-host." The same claim is stated more strongly in `docs/tasks/active/20260902-template-gallery-public-tier-todo.md:142` ("**`doc` needs nothing** — its images already live at the bucket root"). After this change an editor-share-link visitor writes `/api/v1/workspaces/:wid/images/:id` into docs content, so the doc branch's re-hosting pass is now load-bearing rather than a no-op. Behaviour is still correct (the walker does run for `doc` at line 438-440), so this is a stale-contract comment/doc, not a break — but the next reader who trusts it could legitimately delete the pass.

samples.summary: CLI image fetcher snapshots the Authorization value, so it cannot follow `HttpClient`'s JWT refresh — an expired access token silently drops workspace-scoped images from the export instead of retrying
samples.evidence: `packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:294-315` (`send`) rebuilds `this.authHeaders` and retries once after a 401 under `authMode: 'jwt'`, refreshing the session. The image fetcher instead captures a single string at construction time (`packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:341`, `packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:234` — `authorization: authorizationHeader(getConfig(opts))`), and `createImageFetcher` has no refresh path: a 401 on `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/images/:id` just becomes a skipped image (`reportSkippedImage`). So a JWT session that expires between commands (or mid-export) produces an export missing exactly the images this change was added to include, with only a stderr skip note. Fix belongs on the new code: read the credential per hop from the live config, or thread the client's refresh.

samples.summary: The frontend's `docsImageFetcher` has no share-token support, so any docs export reached without a session drops the workspace-scoped images this change introduces
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/export-utils.ts:46-56` fetches every inline `src` with `fetch(resolved, { credentials: 'include' })` and no `?token=`. It is the image fetcher for `exportDocxAndDownload` (`docs/docx-actions.ts:50`), `exportPdfAndDownload` (`docs/pdf-actions.ts:31`) and the slides PDF/PPTX actions. The CLI's sibling fetcher was given a credential in this diff; this one was not. I could not find an export control on the anonymous share route (`DocsExportButton` is mounted only from `packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-detail.tsx:244`, the owner route, where cookies satisfy the gate), so today the gap is unreachable — but the moment a shared/template-preview mount offers export, a share-link-inserted image throws `Image fetch failed: 403` inside the exporter.

samples.summary: Docs canvas thumbnail capture may now silently return no thumbnail, because docs content can hold an auth-gated (cookie-only) workspace image, which the CORS-first/plain-retry loader taints the canvas with
samples.evidence: `packages/docs/src/view/image-cache.ts:78-82` states the CORS-first load is "what lets the template gallery encode a thumbnail of a document containing one" — it holds because a docs `src` was previously the unauthenticated `/images/:id`. A workspace-scoped image (`ApiV1ImageReadController`, `packages/backend/src/api/v1/image-read.controller.ts:92`) authorises by cookie/API key/token, so a `crossOrigin="anonymous"` request from the owner route carries no cookie, fails, and the plain retry (no `crossOrigin`) loads it tainted. `captureThumbnail` → `canvas.toBlob` (`packages/frontend/src/lib/thumbnail-capture.ts:284`) then rejects, and `captureThumbnailId` (`packages/frontend/src/components/template-share-section.tsx:52-67`) swallows it, so publishing a template from such a doc silently loses its card image. Partly pre-existing (cross-workspace re-hosted docs, and sheets/slides already store workspace images), which is why confidence is low — confirming it needs the deployment's actual CORS/cookie behaviour on that route.

samples.summary: Third copy of the image-upload multipart wiring, and a hand-written throttle literal where the image module already exports a shared constant
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/src/image/image.controller.ts:50` uses the shared `@Throttle(IMAGE_THROTTLE)`; the new controller hardcodes `@Throttle({ default: { limit: 30, ttl: 60_000 } })` (line 55) and re-inlines the `FileInterceptor('file', { limits, fileFilter })` block that `image.controller.ts:101-114` and `api/v1/images.controller.ts` already carry verbatim. The byte/MIME constants are shared, so nothing can disagree today, but the wiring is now duplicated in three places and will drift on the next change.

finding.summary: CLI docs export assumes docs images are publicly readable; share-uploaded docs images are workspace-scoped and get silently dropped
finding.evidence: `createImageFetcher` documents and implements the assumption that "Backend's `GET /images/:id` is publicly readable, so we don't attach an Authorization header" (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:737-741), and `packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:333` builds it with `{ serverBase }` only — no credential of any kind. Until this change every docs inline image lived on the unauthenticated `/images/:id` route (see the now-deleted comment in shared-document.tsx and `document-copy.service.ts:432`). After this change an image inserted through an editor share link is stored at `/api/v1/workspaces/{ws}/images/{id}` (image-share-upload.controller.ts:117-121), which `ApiV1ImageReadController.assertCanRead` refuses for an unauthenticated caller. `packages/cli/src/docs/pdf-export.ts:118` and `docx-export.ts:41` pass `reportSkippedImage`/`onImageError`, so the export does not fail — it emits a stderr warning and produces a PDF/DOCX with the image missing. `wafflebase docs export` therefore silently loses exactly the images this feature adds. Fix belongs in the CLI fetcher (attach the configured API key for first-party workspace-image URLs), not in the new controller.

verdict.reason: The described code does not exist in this repository. `ImageFetcherOptions` declares `authorization?: string` (packages/cli/src/docs/image-fetcher.ts:39-51) whose doc comment states the exact opposite of the claimed "publicly readable, so we don't attach an Authorization header" assumption — it names the workspace-scoped, auth-gated `GET /api/v1/workspaces/:wid/images/:id` case and the silent-drop consequence. The fetcher attaches the credential per hop, gated to an exact origin match, at image-fetcher.ts:872-877 (and re-applies it on the proxy retry at :901) via `isConfiguredServerOrigin` (:444-454). Lines 737-744 are `defaultWarn`/`MAX_SKIP_FIELD`, not the quoted comment. The claimed credential-less construction at docs.ts:333 is also absent: packages/cli/src/commands/docs.ts:339-342 passes `authorization: authorizationHeader(getConfig(opts))`, with a comment at :334-338 explaining the share-link workspace-scoped image case. Grep shows the only other call site, packages/cli/src/commands/slides.ts:233-236, passes the same credential, and `authorizationHeader` exists at packages/cli/src/client/http-client.ts:208-216. So there is no site that omits the credential and no image silently dropped — the fix the finding prescribes is already implemented.
